subject: Sprint to Reserve: Mutual Action Plan & Close Timeline
messages:
From: Evan Mills <evan.mills@telescope.health>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@telescope.health
Date: 2026-07-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint to Reserve: MAP & close timeline

Markus — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our engineering and infra leads asked for a concise mutual action plan (MAP) that ties an evaluation window to a reservation commitment for Dedicated/Private capacity. Key constraints on our side: private VPC preferred, target go-live ~2026-10-15, and procurement needs a +/– two week visibility into SKU and commit amounts.

Attached is a light workload profile (Telescope_Initial_Workload_Profile.xlsx) — high-level tokens/day, exemplar prompts, and expected 99th p99 latency targets. For sizing we'd like Redwood's recommendation for a conservative reserve (for steady production) and a staged reserve (tranches) to reduce upfront cost.

Questions:
- Typical lead time for Dedicated H100 pools to be reserved and routable into a private VPC?
- Recommended evaluation cadence and acceptance criteria for us to sign a reservation by mid-September?

Can you put a MAP together with milestones, owners, and procurement-ready SKU list? Evan

Attachment: Telescope_Initial_Workload_Profile.xlsx (Excel, 58 KB)

From: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Mills <evan.mills@telescope.health>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-27T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint to Reserve: MAP & close timeline

Thanks Evan — good framing. I sketched a draft MAP and sizing options below and attached a working doc (MAP-draft-v1.docx) and a quick CSV of GPU sizing scenarios (GPU-Sizing-Options.csv). High level summary first, then timeline.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Evaluation: 4-week focused eval (staging + canary), run your main prompt set and the top 10% longest sequences. Acceptance: p99 latency within 2x target and no functional quality regression on our eval prompts.
- Reservation staging: Reserve 2x H100 (baseline for low-latency production) on Day 0 of commitment, then tranche to 4x H100 by week 6 post-commit once eval is green. Add 2x A100 (or A10) burst nodes for cost-effective throughput if needed.
- Private/VPC lead time: For Private (customer-controlled VPC), provisioning to have runway + routing typically 8–12 weeks from signed order (network peering, KMS integration, SOC2 evidence). Dedicated hosted pockets (Redwood-managed) can be faster (~4–6 weeks).

Proposed MAP milestones (owners):
1) July 27 — Kickoff & workload assumptions final (Evan / Markus)
2) Week 1 (Aug 3) — Staging env provisioned + sample data upload (Priyom / Telescope infra)
3) Weeks 2–5 (Aug 10–Sep 6) — Eval window (3–4 weeks) with weekly check-ins (Neha)
4) Sep 7–13 — Exec signoff & procurement paperwork (Telescope procurement / Lauren)
5) Sep 14 — Commit date: initial reservation (2x H100) placed
6) Oct 15 — Target go-live (scale up to 4x H100 if needed)

Key asks from Telescope:
- Confirm peak concurrency and business SLOs (tokens/day and p50/p95/p99).
- Procurement contact for SOW/PO and any reseller terms.
- Any additional compliance (pen-testing window, logging retention beyond standard).

Notes:
- Cost modeling in GPU-Sizing-Options.csv assumes typical H100 throughput for your prompt mix (approx 1.8–2.2x of A100 on our runtime). We can provide a tranche pricing exhibit for the Sep commit.
- If Procurement requires a guaranteed start date earlier than 8 weeks for Private, we can discuss a Dedicated-to-Private handoff plan to accelerate availability.

I added Priyom and Neha to help run staging and to own the acceptance criteria. I'll circulate a finalized PDF once we align.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.docx, GPU-Sizing-Options.csv

— Markus
Head of Capacity Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Mills <evan.mills@telescope.health>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@telescope.health
Date: 2026-07-27T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint to Reserve: MAP & close timeline

Thanks Markus — that level of detail is perfect. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We prefer a Private deployment in our VPC. Procurement flagged an internal target commit window of Sep 8–15 to hit our Q4 roadmap.
- Target go-live is firm for 2026-10-15 for a public beta; we need at least a 2-week canary in production beforehand.
- Peak concurrency estimate: 150–220 concurrent requests for the conversational path; batch embedding pipelines will run nightly (spiky but modal at 03:00 UTC).
- Compliance: SOC2 + standard pen-test report.

I'll share our procurement timeline doc (attached) with PO cadence and billing constraints. We can accept a staged commit: place 2x H100 on Sep 14 (provisioning start) and tranche up to 4x by Oct 1 if the canary results are green. Please include a firm SKU and lead-time table in the final MAP for our procurement team.

Attachment: Procurement_Timeline.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

— Evan
Director of Engineering, Telescope Health

Subject: Re: Sprint to Reserve: MAP & close timeline — Final MAP (provisional)

Evan / Procurement team — attaching a provisional final MAP (Final-MAP-20260727.pdf) with a procurement-ready SKU table and explicit lead times. Key callouts below and next steps.

Provisional commit plan we will submit to Procurement: 
- SKU table (summary):
  * 2x H100 (reserved) — baseline commit (Sep 14 placement; ~8–12 weeks Private lead time)
  * Burst: 2x A100 (pre-warmed, billed as burst) — optional for nightly throughput
  * Add-on tranche: +2 H100 to reach 4x total (target Oct 1 activation after successful canary)

Lead-time notes:
- Private VPC full provisioning: target 8–12 weeks depending on network peering windows and KMS onboarding. If Telescope needs faster handoff we propose a Dedicated-hosted interim (4–6 weeks) and a controlled migration to Private when networking is ready.
- Hardware availability risk: H100 inventory is constrained for large upfront fleets. The tranche approach minimizes exposure and aligns purchase runway with forecast.

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Functional parity on eval prompt set (redwood eval harness), and p99 latency <= 2x Telescope target in staging; canary in production with 14-day monitoring window with agreed KPIs.

Mutual action items (owners & dates):
- Action 1: Finalize peak load numbers and token shapes — DUE Aug 2 (Evan / Telescope infra)
- Action 2: Staging env + sample data uploaded — DUE Aug 9 (Priyom / Telescope infra)
- Action 3: Eval run + weekly syncs — Aug 10–Sep 6 (Neha / Neha-led check-ins)
- Action 4: Procurement signoff and PO submission — TARGET Sep 8–15 (Telescope procurement / Lauren to coordinate)
- Action 5: Place initial reservation (2x H100) — TARGET Sep 14 (Markus / Finance ops)
- Action 6: Canary start — Sep 28; Canary review complete Oct 12; Go-live Oct 15 if green

Next steps:
1) I will convert the attached PDF into a signature-ready exhibit for your Procurement.
2) Priyom will request staging access details from your infra team (Evan, please share a point-of-contact).
3) Lauren, can Finance prepare a provisional credit hold/approval path to allow us to lock the initial tranche on Sep 14 pending PO?
